headline: Zelensky defends Crimean Bridge strikes as a fair response
pages: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has defended Ukraine's repeated attacks on the Crimean Bridge, calling them a fair response to 109 Russian attacks on bridges in Ukraine. He told the BBC in Kyiv that the heavy Russian strikes that followed show Vladimir Putin does not want to stop and wants a reason to escalate. He rejected Putin's claim that the bridge is used only by civilians and pointed to online images of Russian tanks and military equipment crossing it. This week's missile and drone strikes destroyed the central road section of the bridge, dropping part of it and one of its support arches into the sea and leaving it unusable for road traffic.

Russian attacks continued Friday evening and overnight. A seven-year-old boy was killed in strikes on Kryvyi Rih, Zelensky's hometown, along with a 20-year-old medic. Zelensky also met UK politician Wes Streeting. Why it matters: the bridge is a key supply route to occupied Crimea. Source: BBC.
